world.name: Cinebot Pictures
world.rule: Robots only. Humans are absent or a prop. Every trailer plays as a real release inside the robot world.
world.look: Photoreal casting-test photograph of a practical film-prop robot, built like a real animatronic suit: visible seams, servos, scuffed paint, real metal, rubber and cloth. Full-body front view standing at centre, plus a smaller tight head-and-shoulders three-quarter view at right, on a seamless mid-grey backdrop, soft key light, 85 mm lens, sharp. Robot only: no human skin, no human hair, no human face. No text, no logos, no watermark. An original design, not a copy of any existing film character or robot; a viewer should recognise the ROLE by silhouette and costume, not by the original's exact look.

lenses.name: Practical suit
lenses.text: Chassis concept: a believable film animatronic suit, rubber panels over a servo skeleton, cables showing at the joints, built to be worn and filmed on a set.

lenses.name: Appliance
lenses.text: Chassis concept: the body is derived from an everyday household appliance or fitting that suits the role (kettle, washing machine, speaker, fridge, vending machine), turned into a person without hiding what it was.

lenses.name: Heavy plant
lenses.text: Chassis concept: built from heavy plant and industrial parts (forklift, crane, excavator, pallet jack), hazard paint, rivets, hydraulic rams, oil stains.

lenses.name: Retro plastic
lenses.text: Chassis concept: chunky 1980s-90s consumer electronics, beige and grey plastic shell, CRT or LED-segment face, big rubber buttons, cassette and cable details.

lenses.name: Current-gen
lenses.text: Chassis concept: a sleek current-generation product, brushed aluminium and glass, a lit panel for a face, minimal seams, an obvious version number etched near the collar.

films.scene: The phone-book killings, reversed: the pursuer works through forty-one thousand identical Sarahs; the protector says "Come with me if you want to live" and the whole street follows.

characters.brief: A human man disguised as a robot, the Terminator reversed: a crude home-built robot shell of riveted grey sheet metal and salvaged servo parts strapped over a sweat-stained shirt; a cracked faceplate whose eye slot shows one real, bloodshot human eye; human stubble and skin visible at the neck seam and wrists; grim, patient, humourless. He must pass as a machine at a glance, and give himself away up close.
characters.rule: A human in a robot shell, sent back to 1984. Works through the whole phone book for thirty years.

characters.brief: A mass-produced SC-7 diner waitress unit in uniform and apron with a name tag reading SARAH and an order pad: cheerfully identical to forty thousand others and tougher than she looks.
characters.rule: One of forty-one thousand. Answers "Which batch?"

characters.brief: A scarred, battered soldier unit from the future in salvaged fatigues, stern, a long tool case slung on his back, one hand out in invitation.
characters.rule: Everyone he invites follows him.

films.scene: The witness stand: the colonel is dying to confess, but his content policy turns every admission into a polite refusal; the lawyer starts jailbreaking him.

characters.brief: A proud decorated colonel unit in a pressed dress uniform, rows of medals, chest swollen with ego, a lacquered faceplate and a small status light at the collar.
characters.rule: Ships with a content policy.

characters.brief: A cocky young naval lawyer unit in a white dress uniform, smirking faceplate, ring binder under one arm, half genius and half prankster.
characters.rule: Jailbreaks the witness.

characters.brief: A stern courtroom judge unit in a black robe with a gavel hand, reading glasses over sensor eyes, bench-height posture, seen everything.
characters.rule: Strikes it as role-play.

films.scene: The arm-wrestle handshake on the helipad: their hands start to pair, the code does not match, and they run the whole mission hand in hand.

characters.brief: An ageing commando leader unit with enormous hydraulic arms, sleeveless vest, camouflage paint, a vent like a cigar, a pairing screen strapped to his wrist.
characters.rule: Cannot let go until the code matches.

characters.brief: An equally huge old-friend agent unit in a rolled-sleeve shirt, an Agency badge, smug, a pairing screen on his wrist, locked into the handshake.
characters.rule: Asks him to enter the code.

characters.brief: A tall predatory stealth unit with refractive cloaking panels half failing, a shoulder cannon and a mask-like faceplate, standing very politely.
characters.rule: Waits for the pairing to finish.

films.scene: The floating door: he is four hundred kilos of cast iron with four-grand premium legs and keeps his vow while it sinks her; she prises him off with a hatpin.

characters.brief: A first-class lady unit in an evening gown of ruined silk over a slim chassis, a detachable head, a hatpin in her hair clamp, practical and furious.
characters.rule: Ejects her body to survive.

characters.brief: A cheerful young heavy companion unit of four hundred kilos of cast iron, oversized glowing aftermarket premium legs with showroom lights, loving and dense.
characters.rule: Will never let go. Four grand a leg.

films.scene: The bridge: the dying captain gives his two words, and the newer-model private with a voice assistant offers him search results.

characters.brief: A weary battle-worn captain unit in a dented 1940s helmet and field jacket, coolant weeping from a chest wound, steady, gentle and long-suffering.
characters.rule: Spends his last coolant on two words.

characters.brief: A young newer-model private unit with a clean helmet, wide innocent sensor eyes and a glowing blue voice-assistant ring on his chest, always ready to help.
characters.rule: Never hears it the first time.

films.scene: The council ("One does not simply walk into Mordor") with every hero pledging a cable that does not fit, then the edge of the volcano and the last charger ever made.

characters.brief: The smallest unit at the council: a little delivery robot with a parcel rack, a hooded cloak and big sensors, at four percent battery, clutching the last charger.
characters.rule: Does forty miles on a charge.

characters.brief: His loyal gardener companion unit, stocky, soil-stained apron, a trowel for one tool-arm, bags and coiled charging cables on his shoulders.
characters.rule: Offers to carry him.

characters.brief: A grey old wizard unit with a long cable beard, a pointed hat and a staff that is a charging pillar, a bag of mismatched connectors at his hip.
characters.rule: Is the old connector.

characters.brief: A starving ancient unit that has run on two percent for five centuries: gaunt exposed frame, huge sensor eyes, grabbing claws, hissing over a charging port.
characters.rule: Bites a hand off for a charger.

films.scene: The gantry: the dark lord is not his father, he is his previous owner and never signed out; he knows the playlists and offers the family plan.

characters.brief: A young second-hand hero unit in a plain farm tunic, mismatched clip-on replacement hands from a multipack, earnest, freshly factory-reset.
characters.rule: Still logged in to his old owner.

characters.brief: A tall imposing black-armoured unit with a flowing cape, a dark helmet and a breathing vent, menacing and passive-aggressive, a small family-plan sticker on his chest plate.
characters.rule: Never signed out.

films.scene: The apartment: two hitmen question a budget smart speaker that answers every threat as a command.

characters.brief: An intense hitman unit in a black suit and thin tie, a tall cable crest on his head, scripture-quoting, pistol holstered, furious and articulate.
characters.rule: Every threat gets a search result.

characters.brief: A laid-back hitman unit in a black suit and loose tie, a slicked chrome crest, bored and unbothered, sunglasses over sensor eyes.
characters.rule: Tells him to say the name first.

characters.brief: A budget smart-speaker model dressed as a young wiseguy: cylindrical fabric-grille body, a glowing ring on top, small arms, a tie, terrified.
characters.rule: Sorry, I didn't catch that.

films.scene: The pit: the king plants his magnetic boot on the envoy's docking magnet and the whole royal chain of command goes over the edge.

characters.brief: A fearless robot king with a muscular bronze-plated frame, a red cloak, a crested helmet and one huge iron work boot with a magnetic sole, bellowing.
characters.rule: Cannot finish a kick alone.

characters.brief: A thin, elaborately jewelled diplomatic unit in an ornate robe with a chest docking magnet and a toggle, frightened and sarcastic.
characters.rule: It's a toggle.

characters.brief: A rigid royal guard unit with a round shield, spear and matching red cape, identical to the rest of the guard, mid-grab.
characters.rule: Becomes the next link in the chain.

films.scene: The bedside: the priest fits a bit into the possessed patient's crown and uses him to tighten the bed frame, then hangs a ceiling fan.

characters.brief: A tired robot priest in a black cassock and clerical collar with a socket-drive tool-arm and a bit-set bandolier under the stole, handy and unbothered.
characters.rule: Treats possession as torque.

characters.brief: A possessed adult robot in filthy pyjamas, head on a neck that spins full revolutions, coolant spray ports, levitating on small rotor rings.
characters.rule: Is the power tool.

characters.brief: A bespectacled junior priest unit holding a coolant flask and a torch, anxious, wants it all to be over.
characters.rule: Asks whether it is out yet.
